question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 

A bolt from the blue.

options.text: Sky getting filled with blue light

solution:
The correct answer is **Unexpected and Surprising Event.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the **meaning of the given idiom**:
 
• ** A bolt from the blue: **something important or unusual that happens suddenly or unexpectedly(एकदम अप्रत्याशित).
 
 
• **Example: ***The outbreak of covid-19** ***was a*** bolt from the blue**** catastrophic event in the world.*
 
 
 
• ** **Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3.)***​​​*

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

__
 
• Let's look at the origin of the idiom:__

 
 
• It is a strange phenomenon when lightning strikes during clear daylight far away from the thunderstorm. This uncanny phenomenon is referred to as a **‘bolt from the blue’ **by meteorologists. The lightning bolts can travel several miles from actual thunderstorm clouds, and they then angle downward before striking the earth. So, it is this **unusual phenomenon** that has originated the idiom **“a bolt from the blue". **
